n58b: For the zinc, I'd use zinc carnosine, since it's better tolerated than other forms of zinc and also helps repair leaky gut (Mahmood, et al, 2007). A standard dose is up to 75 mg a day, which holds 16 mg of elemental zinc, and if it causes nausea, take less at a time. Zinc can lower your copper over time, so I'd also take 1–2 mg of elemental copper a day, as copper gluconate or citrate (not cupric oxide, which is poorly absorbed). For L-serine, I'd do 5–15 g a day, depending how it feels. Higher doses bring more GI distress, though up to 30 g a day has been used in trials for neurodegenerative conditions (Levine, et al, 2017).
